transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thanks for seeing me. Um, well, I guess the main reason I'm here is... well, it's not a huge deal, I don't think, but people keep telling me I'm not listening. Like, my supervisor at the plant, or my wife, they'll be talking right to me, and... I don't know, a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which I know is annoying. I really try to pay attention, I promise I do, but it just sort of slips away. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.

When people are talking to you and you miss part of what they say, is it because you have trouble actually hearing or making out their words clearly, or do you hear them fine but your mind seems to wander or drift elsewhere?

Oh, no, my hearing is definitely fine. We have to do those hearing tests at the plant every year for safety, and I always do great on them. So I know I can hear the words just fine. 

But... um, as for my mind wandering, I'm not really sure? I don't feel like I'm daydreaming or anything like that, and I'm definitely not ignoring them on purpose. I really do want to hear what they're saying, I swear. It's just... I don't know, it just sort of fades out for a second and I realize I missed it. 

I hope I'm not being too confusing? I just honestly haven't really noticed exactly what my brain is doing when it happens. I hope that's an okay answer.

During these moments when you miss part of what someone is saying, has anyone ever noticed you staring blankly, pausing mid-action, or making any unusual movements, and do you ever feel like you 'lost time' or can't recall a few seconds?

No, nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I definitely don't stare off into space or freeze up or anything weird like that. I'm usually pretty active, always moving around or doing something with my hands, so I don't think I ever just pause mid-action. 

And I definitely don't feel like I lose time. It's really just that I miss a few words here and there, you know? It's nothing scary like blacking out or forgetting where I am. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Would you say you've had this kind of trouble tuning in and catching what people say for as long as you can remember, even back in school, or is this something that's really only started or gotten noticeably worse recently?

Well, I guess... um, it's always been this way, honestly. Even back when I was a kid. But it wasn't really a bad thing, you know? I mean, I just had a lot of energy. 

I remember in elementary school, my teachers were always moving my desk around because I just... I couldn't really stay in my seat for too long. And I'd get so excited about knowing the answers that I'd just sort of blurt them out before I was called on. I guess I got in a little trouble sometimes for, you know, kind of jumping into what the other kids were doing. But I was just trying to help, really! 

So, yeah, it's been going on since before middle school. But I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid or anything? I was just really eager, I promise. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Besides these listening lapses, do you still notice things like restlessness, fidgeting, or blurting things out impulsively now as an adult, in multiple areas of your life such as work and home?

Well... um, yeah, I guess I do still do those things. I just always like to keep busy and keep things moving, you know? But... 

To be completely honest, and I really hate to admit this because I don't want you to think poorly of me... it's actually been causing some real trouble lately. At the plant, I've... well, I've gotten some formal warnings. I get a bit ahead of myself or rush things, and... well, I worry a lot that I could actually lose my job, or worse, cause a real safety problem on the line. I'm a really hard worker, I swear! I just have a hard time slowing down.

And at home... I try so hard to be a good dad and a good husband. But my wife and the kids, they get pretty frustrated with me. I want to help them out, but I guess I end up just disrupting their routines instead of actually helping things run smoothly. I'll jump in to do something and just end up making it more chaotic. 

I feel awful about it, honestly. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible guy or a bad employee? I really am trying my best to do right by everybody. Is... is that the kind of information you needed? I hope I answered that okay.

Have you ever had periods lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt on top of the world, separate from your usual pattern of restlessness and impulsivity?

No, no, I've never had anything like that. I mean, I'm always pretty energetic, like I said, but it's just my normal everyday speed. I don't get these... days-long spells where I feel on top of the world or stop sleeping. 

I definitely still need my sleep! I try to get a good night's rest so I can be ready for my shift at the plant. I don't want you to think I'm, you know, staying up for days or acting wild or anything. It's just the regular restlessness, nothing extreme like what you're describing. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, did teachers or family members already notice you having trouble paying attention, sitting still, or acting impulsively at that age?

Well, um... yeah, like I mentioned a little earlier, it was definitely happening back then. Even before middle school. I really hope I don't sound like a broken record, but... yeah, teachers were always moving my seat around because I just couldn't stay put. 

And, you know, I was just so eager to participate that I'd call out the answers without raising my hand. I guess I did get into a little bit of trouble for butting into other kids' work, too. But I really didn't mean any harm by it! I was just trying to be helpful and get involved. I wasn't trying to be a troublemaker, I promise. 

I hope it's okay that I brought that up again? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need to figure this out. Did I explain that alright?
